# PathwaySeeker

> PathwaySeeker checks the steps of metabolic pathways proposed by an AI assistant (Claude Code, Codex or other MCP clients) against a graph of KEGG reactions linked to the enzymes and metabolites detected in an organism's proteomics and metabolomics data. Each step is labeled as found in the graph (consistent with the data, not proof that the reaction occurs) or as a hypothesis (not found in the graph, not ruled out). Described in a bioRxiv preprint (2026, not peer reviewed) from Pacific Northwest National Laboratory.

## Start here
- [README](https://github.com/pnnl/PathwaySeeker/blob/master/README.md): what it does, five-minute setup, using your own data
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/pnnl/PathwaySeeker/blob/master/AGENTS.md): step-by-step setup instructions for AI assistants
- [Skill](https://github.com/pnnl/PathwaySeeker/blob/master/skills/pathwayseeker/SKILL.md): how an assistant builds graphs and answers questions

## Reference
- [Evaluation](https://github.com/pnnl/PathwaySeeker/blob/master/evals/README.md): evaluation queries, grader, results and training data from the paper; scoring rubric and results
- [Preprint](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.04.14.718256v1): PathwaySeeker: Evidence-Grounded AI Reasoning over Organism-Specific Metabolic Networks

## Topics
multi-omics, proteomics, metabolomics, metabolic pathways, metabolic network reconstruction, KEGG, knowledge graph, LLM agents, Model Context Protocol (MCP), Claude Code, Codex, non-model organisms, Trametes versicolor
